hook.narration: You have been doing physics since you learned to walk. Here is the proof.

cards.label: Definition
cards.title: Motion is a change of position

rows.text: Something moves when its position changes
No change of position, no motion

cards.note: Every time you walk, run, or ride a bus, you are doing physics.
cards.narration: Motion simply means a change of position. If something moves from one place to another, it is in motion. If its position does not change, it is not moving, no matter how complicated it looks.

cards.label: Key idea
cards.title: Motion is relative

rows.text: Sitting still? You are moving with the Earth
Motion always needs a reference point

cards.note: The Earth circles the Sun at about 30 kilometers every second.
cards.narration: Here is the key idea. Motion is relative. You say an object moves by comparing it to a reference point. Right now you are sitting still, but relative to the Sun you are moving at about thirty kilometers every second.

cards.label: Examples
cards.title: Motion, or not?
cards.note: A tree's position never changes, so it is not in motion.
cards.narration: Quick check. Walking to school, that is motion. A bus moving on the street, motion. A spinning fan, motion. A tree standing in the yard, no motion, because its position never changes.
